status_rule: proven only if the identified model's held-out arm error is lower than both the default model's and the fair baseline's with the 95% interval of each paired improvement above zero

joint_map.assumption: Sign +1 and the rest pose shared: every episode starts with the arm folded at rest, which the Menagerie file

shoulder_pan.title: second-order servo with delay, angle-dependent offset

shoulder_lift.title: second-order servo with delay, deadband, angle-dependent offset

elbow_flex.title: first-order lag with delay, deadband, angle-dependent offset

wrist_flex.title: first-order lag with delay, speed limit

gripper.title: first-order lag with delay, deadband
gripper.mjcf: not written: Menagerie defaults kept (contact with objects; law at its bounds)

identified_model.what: the identified MJCF (so_arm100_identified.xml) driven by the logged command plus each joint's command offset: b and, where chosen, the angle-dependent offset, minus the recentring measured on the training episodes

fair_baseline.what: the default model with one command delay for all joints, chosen on the training episodes by MuJoCo replay

stronger_baseline.what: the fair baseline plus a constant per-joint offset (mean measured minus commanded angle on the training episodes)

limits: only the motions in these 50 pick-and-place episodes (speeds up to about 170 deg/s); payloads, wear, temperature and other units of the arm are not covered
the measured angle is the arm's own encoder reading, so the identified delay includes the bus and logging latency; that is the delay a replay of logged commands needs
the gripper closes on objects that the simulator scene does not contain, so it is reported but not counted in the arm total
the map from logged degrees to model radians is an assumption (see model.joint_map); it only moves where gravity acts, and heldout_comparison.gravity_effect_on_default shows how much that matters
